For the anti-nutritional compound to disappear you have to abolish, or at least severely cripple, the activity of the biosynthetic enzyme that this gene encodes.  
Among the four EMS-induced alleles the one that is most likely to do so is the allele that introduces an early nonsense (stop-codon) mutation near the start of the ORF; this will either

1. produce a protein of only two amino-acid residues, which cannot be functional, or  
2. trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (the premature stop lies in exon 1 and several exon–exon junctions remain downstream), so little or no protein is made at all.

Inspection of the mutant sequences in the correct reading frame:

• Mutant 1 …ATG TTC TAC GCT… – only two missense changes (Phe→Phe is silent; Leu→Tyr is missense). Protein is almost full length → function likely retained.  
• Mutant 3 …ATG TTT TAC GCT GGT GTC… – several missense changes but no stop or frameshift → protein probably still partly functional.  
• Mutant 4 …ATG TTT TAC GCT ACT TCT… – again just missense substitutions; no frameshift or premature stop in-frame.  
• Mutant 2 …ATG TTC TAA GCT… – “TAA’’ is a stop codon at the third codon of the ORF → very early truncation/NMD.

Therefore Mutant 2 is, by far, the most likely to abolish enzyme activity and eliminate the undesirable compound.

Answer: D
